dual-encoder-two-tower.title: Dual-encoder (two-tower)
dual-encoder-two-tower.description: Encodes each TF and gene independently, then scores the pair via cosine similarity of the two encodings.

cross-encoder-joint.title: Cross-encoder
cross-encoder-joint.description: Concatenates TF-gene features and processes them jointly through shared layers before scoring, allowing direct feature interaction.

balanced-baseline.title: Balanced (1:1) baseline
balanced-baseline.description: Cross-encoder scores 0.9025 AUROC versus 0.7941 for the dual-encoder, a 10.84pp gap even with identical parameter counts — later traced by <inode id="joint-encoding-ablation">ablation to joint encoding itself</inode> rather than any specific interaction term.

moderate-imbalance-5-1-10-1.title: Moderate imbalance (5:1, 10:1)
moderate-imbalance-5-1-10-1.description: The dual-encoder degrades to roughly 0.694 and 0.658 AUROC while the cross-encoder stays near 0.911, widening the gap to over 25pp at 10:1.

severe-imbalance.title: Severe imbalance (50:1)
severe-imbalance.description: The dual-encoder collapses entirely at this realistic ratio, while the cross-encoder remains stable, a critical difference for real regulatory databases dominated by non-interacting pairs.

joint-encoding-ablation.title: Joint encoding vs interaction term
joint-encoding-ablation.description: Ablation shows 95% of the cross-encoder's AUROC advantage comes from processing the pair jointly, with only 5% attributable to the element-wise product interaction term.

structured-pruning.title: Structured neuron pruning
structured-pruning.description: Both architectures tolerate at least 60% neuron removal without post-hoc performance loss, indicating substantial over-parameterization at 5.58M.

effective-rank-analysis.title: Effective rank analysis
effective-rank-analysis.description: Measures the intrinsic dimensionality of each model's learned representations to gauge representational efficiency.

cold-start-eval.title: Cold-start evaluation
cold-start-eval.description: The dual-encoder's <inode id="dual-encoder-two-tower">independently encoded TF and gene representations</inode> give it a modest edge generalizing to unseen TFs or genes, since it doesn't rely solely on pair-specific learning.

transductive-limitation.title: Transductive limitation
transductive-limitation.description: The cross-encoder's <inode id="cross-encoder-joint">joint processing of concatenated TF-gene features</inode> is inherently transductive, but this rarely matters in practice since most GRN inference tasks already know the entities involved.

expression-baseline.title: Expression-only baseline
expression-baseline.description: A feature-based baseline with no learned embeddings contextualizes how much the neural architectures contribute over simple expression matching.

double-sigmoid-vanishing-gradients.title: Double-Sigmoid Vanishing Gradients
double-sigmoid-vanishing-gradients.description: The model squashed its own learning signal twice in the backward pass, leaving almost nothing left to learn from.

unstable-gradient-estimator.title: Unstable Gradient Estimator
unstable-gradient-estimator.description: A numerically shaky math shortcut produced noisy, unreliable gradient updates during training.

gradient-clipping-fix.title: Missing Gradient Clipping
gradient-clipping-fix.description: Updates had no cap on how large they could grow, so some blew up and derailed training entirely.

two-tower-modular-mlp.title: Two-Tower (Modular MLP)
two-tower-modular-mlp.description: Separate entity and expression encoders combined via dot-product similarity, allowing precomputed representations for fast retrieval.

cross-encoder-monolithic-mlp.title: Cross-Encoder (Monolithic MLP)
cross-encoder-monolithic-mlp.description: Concatenates TF and gene features up front and processes the pair jointly through a shared MLP.

shared-training-setup.title: Shared Training Setup
shared-training-setup.description: Both architectures use per-batch Adam with <inode id="gradient-clipping-fix">gradient clipping at a threshold of 5.0</inode> and stable numerics, isolating architecture as the only remaining variable.

human-brain-scrna-seq.title: Human Brain scRNA-seq Dataset
human-brain-scrna-seq.description: 47,388 transcription factor–gene pairs drawn from single-cell RNA-seq data of the human brain.

balanced-vs-imbalanced-training.title: Balanced vs 5:1 Imbalanced Training
balanced-vs-imbalanced-training.description: A fair 1:1 positive:negative split is compared against a harder 5:1 split that mirrors how rare true regulatory links are in real biology.

metrics-and-seeds.title: Metrics and Seeds
metrics-and-seeds.description: Accuracy, F1, and AUROC are measured over five random seeds with bootstrap confidence intervals.

balanced-accuracy-and-auroc.title: Balanced Accuracy and AUROC
balanced-accuracy-and-auroc.description: Under the <inode id="balanced-vs-imbalanced-training">fair 1:1 positive:negative split</inode>, the cross-encoder reaches 83.03% accuracy and 0.904 AUROC versus the two-tower's 80.90% accuracy and 0.810 AUROC.

imbalance-degradation.title: Imbalance Degradation
imbalance-degradation.description: At the <inode id="balanced-vs-imbalanced-training">harder 5:1 imbalanced split</inode> the two-tower loses 6.87 percentage points of accuracy, while the cross-encoder loses only 1.56 points.

architecture-not-bugs-drives-the-remaini.title: Architecture, Not Bugs, Drives the Remaining Gap
architecture-not-bugs-drives-the-remaini.description: After correcting all three gradient bugs, the cross-encoder's joint processing of TF-gene pairs still wins, showing the gap is architectural, not just buggy code.

tf-gene-pairs.title: 47,388 TF-gene pairs
tf-gene-pairs.description: Human brain scRNA-seq data paired with regulatory ground truth, split 70/15/15 into training, validation, and test sets.

dorothea-trrust-priors.title: DoRothEA & TRRUST priors
dorothea-trrust-priors.description: Two curated transcription-factor-target databases supply the ground-truth regulatory links used as labels for the prediction task.

entity-tower.title: Entity tower (512-d embeddings)
entity-tower.description: Learns a 512-dimensional embedding for each transcription factor and gene, passed through three fully connected layers with batch normalization and dropout.

expression-tower.title: Expression tower (11-d profiles)
expression-tower.description: Encodes an 11-dimensional cell-type mean expression profile through the same three-layer structure, capturing cell-type-specific activity.

temp-scaled-dot-product.title: Temperature-scaled dot product (tau = 0.05)
temp-scaled-dot-product.description: Interaction scores come from a dot-product similarity between tower outputs, scaled by a temperature of 0.05 and passed through a sigmoid.

adam-l2-training.title: Adam optimizer + L2 regularization
adam-l2-training.description: Trained with the Adam optimizer, L2 regularization (lambda = 0.01), and early stopping with 10-epoch patience.

pure-rust-implementation.title: Pure-Rust implementation
pure-rust-implementation.description: Built from scratch without PyTorch, TensorFlow, or any deep learning framework, forcing explicit numerical decisions that aided reproducibility.

five-model-ensemble.title: 5-model ensemble
five-model-ensemble.description: Averaging predicted probabilities across five independently trained models lifts accuracy from 80.14% to 83.06%.

cross-seed-variance.title: Cross-seed variance (CV = 2.06%)
cross-seed-variance.description: Re-running training from different random initializations produced only 2.06% coefficient of variation, a stability the <inode id="pure-rust-implementation">pure-Rust, framework-free numerics</inode> likely helped enforce.

hyperparameter-tuning-16-1-pp.title: Hyperparameter tuning (+16.1 pp)
hyperparameter-tuning-16-1-pp.description: Careful hyperparameter tuning alone accounted for 77% of the total accuracy improvement, more than any architectural change.

83-06-accuracy-0-844-auroc.title: 83.06% accuracy, 0.844 AUROC
83-06-accuracy-0-844-auroc.description: The <inode id="five-model-ensemble">five-model ensemble</inode> reaches 83.06% accuracy and an AUROC of 0.844 on the 47,388-pair human brain test set.

gcan-accuracy-f1-paradox.title: GCAN's accuracy-F1 paradox
gcan-accuracy-f1-paradox.description: GCAN, a cross-attention baseline, scores a higher 91% accuracy but only a 0.692 F1-score, missing many true regulatory links due to poor recall on imbalanced data.
